1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
3	# ║  plugin-registry — lifecycle hook dispatch + fail-closed output scanner    ║
4	# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
5	#
6	# Split from registry.sh (#364). Owns the runtime dispatch path:
7	# `plugin_hook_call` (sources plugin.sh in an isolated subshell, applies
8	# pre-source tamper checks, calls the hook function, then verifies declared
9	# outputs) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (ADR-001 fail-closed artifact-presence
10	# scanner). Depends on yaml_get / verify_plugin_for_source from the other two
11	# split modules — sourced together via the registry.sh facade.
12	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail.
13	
14	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
15	_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED=1
16	
17	# #1809 (ADR-058 C9): declared-output path resolution is shared with
18	# core/pipeline/write-boundary.sh so the artifact scanner and the write-boundary
19	# classifier can never disagree about where a declared output lives.
20	# shellcheck source=output-paths.sh
21	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/output-paths.sh"
22	# shellcheck source=write-ownership.sh
23	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/write-ownership.sh"
24	# shellcheck source=attempt-archive.sh
25	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/attempt-archive.sh"
26	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh
27	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh"
28	
29	# ─── scan_plugin_outputs — fail-closed artifact-presence scanner (#288) ─────
30	# ADR-001 §Fail-closed scanner contract:
31	#   "If a plugin declares an output but no artifact exists at outputs[].path
32	#    after run completes with exit 0, the engine emits a synthetic blocking
33	#    finding."
34	# #1906 retired provides.artifact_type, which the original wording keyed on;
35	# outputs[].required is the single declaration the scan now honours.
36	#
37	# Arguments:
38	#   $1 — plugin_dir
39	#   $2 — state_file (so $state_dir / $artifacts_dir can substitute into paths)
40	#
41	# Returns:
42	#   0 if all declared outputs are present (or no outputs declared).
43	#   1 if any declared output is missing — and emits one
44	#      `plugin.artifact.missing` event per missing path.
45	#
46	# Path-template substitution (Phase 0.5): supports ${state_dir} and
47	# ${artifact_dir} / ${artifacts_dir}. Any other ${VAR} resolves from the work
48	# unit's exported environment (#1803) — per-member outputs such as review-lens's
49	# `lens-${ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID}.json` (ADR-047 §2) are only checkable once the
50	# element var is expanded. A var that is unset stays literal and fails the check.
51	scan_plugin_outputs() {
52	    local plugin_dir="$1"
53	    local state_file="${2:-}"
54	    local stage="${3:-}"
55	    # #2252: `probe` answers present-or-not with no events, findings or marker.
56	    local probe="${4:-}"
57	    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
58	
59	    # No manifest, no outputs to scan — silently succeed.
60	    [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]] && return 0
61	
62	    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id" 2>/dev/null || true)"
63	    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true)"
64	    # ADR-047 §4 capability flag: build legitimately writes a zero-byte diff.patch
65	    # when a turn changed no code. The exemption is deliberately narrow — it never
66	    # covers a `primary: true` output, so a stage cannot mask an empty verdict
67	    # artifact (e.g. build-summary.json) by declaring the flag in its own manifest.
68	    local empty_diff_ok; empty_diff_ok="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.empty_diff_legitimate" 2>/dev/null || true)"
69	
70	    # Compute substitution roots from state_file.
71	    local state_dir="" artifact_dir=""
72	    if [[ -n "$state_file" ]]; then
73	        state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"
74	        artifact_dir="${state_dir}/artifacts"
75	    fi
76	
77	    # Pull outputs[].path entries from the manifest. yaml_get/yaml_get_list
78	    # don't model lists of objects, so grep the YAML directly. Format we
79	    # support (per ADR-001):
80	    #   outputs:
81	    #     - name: foo
82	    #       path: ${artifact_dir}/foo.json
83	    #       type: foo.json
84	    # #511 F2: respect `required: false` on outputs. Without this, the scanner
85	    # would flag a legitimately optional artifact as a fail-closed contract
86	    # violation. (test_failures_summary was the original example; ADR-055 §9
87	    # since made it `required: true` — a summary is published on every terminal
88	    # verdict, so its absence IS a violation now.)
89	    local paths
90	    paths="$(_registry_output_path_rows "$manifest")"
91	
92	    [[ -z "$paths" ]] && return 0
93	
94	    local missing=0
95	    local raw_path raw_primary resolved _violation _event
96	    while IFS=$'\t' read -r raw_path raw_primary; do
97	        [[ -z "$raw_path" ]] && continue
98	        resolved="$(_registry_resolve_output_path "$raw_path" "$state_dir" "$artifact_dir")"
99	
100	        # An absent output always violates; a zero-byte one violates unless the
101	        # plugin declared the empty-diff capability AND this is not its primary.
102	        _violation=""
103	        if [[ ! -e "$resolved" ]]; then
104	            _violation="absent"
105	            _event="plugin.artifact.missing"
106	        elif [[ ! -s "$resolved" ]] &&
107	             ! { [[ "$empty_diff_ok" == "true" ]] && [[ "$raw_primary" != "true" ]]; }; then
108	            _violation="empty"
109	            _event="plugin.artifact.empty"
110	        fi
111	
112	        if [[ -n "$_violation" && "$probe" == "probe" ]]; then
113	            return 1
114	        fi
115	        if [[ -n "$_violation" ]]; then
116	            if [[ "$_violation" == "absent" ]]; then
117	                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output missing: $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
118	            else
119	                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output is empty (zero bytes): $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
120	            fi
121	            emit_event "$_event" \
122	                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
123	                "kind=$kind" \
124	                "expected_path=$resolved" \
125	                "template=$raw_path"
126	            # ADR-001 §Fail-closed contract: emit plugin.contract.violated and write
127	            # synthetic blocking findings.json so the output stage can surface the violation.
128	            local _stage_id="${stage:-${plugin_id}}"
129	            emit_event "plugin.contract.violated" \
130	                "stage=$_stage_id" \
131	                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
132	                "expected_path=$resolved" \
133	                "reason=artifact_missing_or_empty"
134	            if [[ -n "$state_dir" ]]; then
135	                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/artifacts"
136	                local _findings_file="${state_dir}/artifacts/${_stage_id}-${plugin_id}-contract-violated-findings.json"
137	                jq -n \
138	                    --arg stage "$_stage_id" \
139	                    --arg plugin "$plugin_id" \
140	                    --arg path "$resolved" \
141	                    --arg violation "$_violation" \
142	                    '{
143	                        schema_version: 1,
144	                        findings: [{
145	                            id: "artifact-contract-violated",
146	                            title: ("Plugin contract violated: " + $plugin +
147	                                    (if $violation == "empty"
148	                                     then " wrote an empty (zero-byte) required output"
149	                                     else " declared a required output but wrote no artifact" end)),
150	                            severity: "blocking",
151	                            stage: $stage,
152	                            plugin: $plugin,
153	                            detail: ("Expected artifact at: " + $path)
154	                        }]
155	                    }' > "$_findings_file" 2>/dev/null || true
156	                # #1809: file-backed marker so runner_read_stage_disposition (a separate
157	                # process under map:) can detect the violation and return broken.
158	                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/runtime"
159	                touch "${state_dir}/runtime/artifact-contract-violated" 2>/dev/null || true
160	            fi
161	            missing=$((missing + 1))
162	        fi
163	    done <<< "$paths"
164	
165	    return $((missing > 0))
166	}
167	
168	# ─── _lc_owned_by_others_deny <state_dir> <stage> (#2189) ────────────────────
169	# One absolute path per line: every file a stage OTHER than <stage> reported
170	# owning (artifacts/stage-reports.json). Empty when nothing is owned.
171	_lc_owned_by_others_deny() {
172	    local rec="${1:-}/artifacts/stage-reports.json" me="${2:-}"
173	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || return 0
174	    # Read without a fork: nothing owned (most runs) needs no jq at all.
175	    local _body; _body="$(<"$rec")"
176	    [[ "$_body" == *'"owned_files"'* ]] || return 0
177	    jq -r --arg me "$me" --arg root "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}" '
178	        [(.owned_files // {}) | to_entries[] | select(.key != $me) | .value[] | "\($root)/\(.)"]
179	        | unique[]' <<< "$_body" 2>/dev/null
180	}
181	
182	# ─── plugin_hook_call ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
183	# Source the plugin's plugin.sh and call a lifecycle hook by name.
184	# Plugin functions are isolated by sub-shell to prevent namespace pollution.
185	plugin_hook_call() {
186	    local plugin_dir="$1"
187	    local hook_name="$2"   # run | cleanup (or kind-specific)
188	    shift 2
189	    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
190	    local plugin_sh="$plugin_dir/plugin.sh"
191	
192	    # ADR-068 §8: mark when this run of the stage started, FIRST — before any
193	    # refusal below can return — so a run that writes no result, refused or
194	    # not, is never credited with the previous run's (stage_result_is_current).
195	    [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && stage_dispatch_mark "${2:-}" "${1:-}"
196	
197	    if [[ ! -f "$plugin_sh" ]]; then
198	        error "plugin_hook_call: plugin.sh missing: $plugin_sh"
199	        return 1
200	    fi
201	
202	    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id")"
203	    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind")"
204	
205	    # ADR-054 §3 (#1862): the engine states, for exactly the span of one
206	    # dispatch, which stage this is and which plugin serves it.
207	    #
208	    # A plugin IS self-defining about what it is — plugin-bootstrap.sh resolves
209	    # _ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR from its own BASH_SOURCE, and 18 plugins do. It can
210	    # never be self-defining about which STAGE it is: `review_lenses`
211	    # (simple.yaml) is served by plugin `review-lens` via role `review_lens` —
212	    # three namespaces the template alone maps, and under `map:` all six lens
213	    # members receive that one stage name. Everything keyed to the flow (the
214	    # timeline, stage_statuses, the per-stage router knobs) needs the stage
215	    # name; introspection can only ever yield the plugin id.
216	    #
217	    # `local -x`, not `export`, for three reasons: it reaches the emit_event
218	    # calls below, which fire OUTSIDE the plugin subshell (the blank envelope
219	    # .plugin/.kind of #1705); it reaches the subshell and anything it spawns;
220	    # and it unsets on return, so stage N's identity cannot bleed into stage
221	    # N+1 — a plain export would trade a blank field for a stale one.
222	    #
223	    # This is the only site that reaches all four dispatch arms. The `map:` arm
224	    # runs a generated standalone script (strategies/common.sh) the runner
225	    # cannot export into — but plugin_hook_call is its last line.
226	    #
227	    # ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is deliberately NOT set: it is an operator override
228	    # every reader spells `${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-<default>}`, and ADR-024 /
229	    # persona-resolve.sh forbid relying on it as a root. Derive from
230	    # ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR instead.
231	    #
232	    # Stage id is $1 post-shift for both hooks — run(stage_id, state_file, ...)
233	    # and cleanup(stage_id, state_file, scope), ADR-054 §2. Same assumption
234	    # scan_plugin_outputs already makes below.
235	    #
236	    # `:-` is deliberate and deliberately unlike `stage_arg="${1:-}"` below: an
237	    # empty $1 keeps the ambient stage rather than blanking it. A caller with no
238	    # stage to name must not erase the one its own caller established — the
239	    # throttle marker's path is keyed on this value and is written inside the
240	    # dispatch but read outside it (router-rc-classify.sh:154), so a blank here
241	    # would split the key across the boundary. scan_plugin_outputs has no such
242	    # cross-boundary reader and wants the literal argument.
243	    local -x ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE="${1:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
244	    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): the unit's own name — the stage, or <stage>.<element>
245	    # for a map member — for this dispatch only. The element is consumed here, so
246	    # a stage dispatched from inside the member is named by its own stage.
247	    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE}${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT:+.${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT}}"
248	    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT=""
249	    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN="$plugin_id"
250	    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND="$kind"
251	    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR="$plugin_dir"
252	
253	    # ADR-058 §2 (#1918): the engine states WHERE this stage may write, for
254	    # exactly the span of one dispatch. #1809 makes a declared output a write
255	    # boundary; a boundary cannot be enforced until the permitted areas are
256	    # defined, and the per-stage scratch area did not exist at all.
257	    #
258	    # Same site and same `local -x` as the identity block above, for the same
259	    # reasons: it is the only site reaching all four dispatch arms (the `map:`
260	    # arm runs a generated standalone script the runner cannot export into, and
261	    # this call is that script's last line), and `local -x` restores the prior
262	    # value AND the prior export attribute on return, so stage N's scratch
263	    # cannot bleed into stage N+1 and the test harness's sandboxed
264	    # ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR (scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh) comes back intact.
265	    #
266	    # Guarded on `$2` being an ABSOLUTE path — the state_file, post-shift, per
267	    # ADR-054 §2, the same argument scan_plugin_outputs reads below.
268	    #
269	    # Absolute, not merely non-empty, and the difference is load-bearing.
270	    # `dirname` of a bare relative name is `.`, and by the time a stage
271	    # dispatches, the runner has cd'd into the RUN'S WORKTREE (ADR-052) — so a
272	    # relative state_file would put `scratch/` and `artifacts/` inside the
273	    # repository under change. That is the exact leak this block exists to close,
274	    # reintroduced by the block itself.
275	    #
276	    # It cannot happen from the engine: runner.sh absolutizes state_dir "BEFORE
277	    # anything derives a path from state_dir" precisely so no caller has to think
278	    # about this (ADR-052, #1640). A relative or empty `$2` therefore means an
279	    # ad-hoc caller — the `plugin_hook_call … ""` of
280	    # tests/unit/plugin-lifecycle-event-balance-test.sh, or the positional
281	    # `… "arg1" "arg2"` of tests/integration/core-plugin-registry-test.sh — which
282	    # has no job folder to be inside and must reach the plugin with the
283	    # environment it has today.
284	    #
285	    # Setting TMPDIR is the load-bearing part. scripts/lib/env-scrub.sh
286	    # wildcard-unsets every ZBUILD_* before each model spawn — with the
287	    # unset-until-gone loop #1873 added specifically to defeat `local -x`
288	    # layering at this seam — while TMPDIR is explicitly PRESERVED. It is
289	    # therefore the only channel that reaches the model. Redirecting it puts the
290	    # model's own temp writes in bounds and relocates every `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`
291	    # consumer in the engine and the plugins with zero plugin edits.
292	    #
293	    # ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR is a definition, not a leak fix: the gate plugins test
294	    # for a live state file first and only fall back to temp when invoked
295	    # ad-hoc, so their outputs land correctly today. What changes is that the
296	    # plugin's own fallback and scan_plugin_outputs' `${artifact_dir}`
297	    # substitution below become the same directory BY CONSTRUCTION, instead of
298	    # two independent derivations that a caller can silently split.
299	    if [[ "${2:-}" == /* ]]; then
300	        local _ws_state_dir; _ws_state_dir="$(dirname "$2")"
301	        local -x ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR="${_ws_state_dir}/artifacts"
302	
303	        # #2022: the acceptance TESTFILES belong to the stage that AUTHORS them.
304	        # Every other spawn is denied Edit() on them, so build cannot rewrite an
305	        # assertion to agree with its own implementation. Derived from the role
306	        # the plugin declares, never from a stage id: naming `build` here would
307	        # be a stage naming a stage, the shape #1767 removed from routing.
308	        # core/router/permissions.sh renders the rules; the decision is here.
309	        local -x ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT=""
310	        # #2170: `$1` here is the STAGE ID — the function `shift 2`s its
311	        # plugin_dir/hook_name arguments away above. Looked up on the stage id
312	        # the role was always empty, so the author was denied its own testfiles
313	        # (invisible while the rule rendered as `Edit(/abs)`, #2163).
314	        # #2189: files ANOTHER stage reported owning (test-author reports the
315	        # testfiles it authored) — from the run's stage-reports record, never
316	        # design.md by path and never a role name. The owner is not denied.
317	        ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$(_lc_owned_by_others_deny "$_ws_state_dir" "${1:-}")"
318	        [[ -n "$ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT" ]] && ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+=$'\n'
319	
320	        # #2174: write ownership from the manifests (write-ownership.sh) —
321	        # other plugins' declared outputs, and the repo unless declared.
322	        _lc_other_outputs_deny "$plugin_dir" "$_ws_state_dir"   # parent shell: fills the memo
323	        ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$_LC_DENY_OUT"
324	        local _lc_wr; _lc_wr="$(manifest_index_get "$manifest" capabilities.writes_repository 2>/dev/null)" \
325	            || _lc_wr="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.writes_repository" 2>/dev/null || true)"
326	        if [[ "${_lc_wr%$'\n'}" != "true" ]]; then
327	            _lc_repo_entries_deny "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}"
328	            ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$_LC_DENY_OUT"
329	        fi
330	
331	        if ! declare -F stage_scratch_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1; then
332	            # shellcheck source=../pipeline/stage-scratch.sh
333	            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../pipeline" && pwd)/stage-scratch.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
334	        fi
335	        if declare -F stage_scratch_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1; then
336	            local _ws_scratch
337	            # Fail-open: an unnameable stage or an uncreatable directory leaves
338	            # both vars unset and every consumer on the fallback it has today.
339	            # A stage must not be refused dispatch because scratch was
340	            # unavailable — that would make a diagnostic convenience a new way
341	            # for a run to die.
342	            if _ws_scratch="$(stage_scratch_ensure "$_ws_state_dir" "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}" 2>/dev/null)" \
343	               && [[ -n "$_ws_scratch" ]]; then
344	                local -x ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH="$_ws_scratch"
345	                local -x TMPDIR="$_ws_scratch"
346	            fi
347	        fi

463	    # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): mark the dispatch start so write_boundary_check can

478	    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.start" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
479	
480	    # Run in a subshell to isolate plugin's variables/functions.
481	    # For the "run" hook: arm a per-dispatch watchdog so a hung stage is killed at
482	    # stage_timeout_s (issue #1801, SPEC-1/SPEC-2). Precedence: template
483	    # _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage> > ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S env > 5400 s default.
484	    local rc=0
485	    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
486	        if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then

499	            # process group (created by set -m + & above). Any background job the

112	_usage() {

114	    cat >&2 <<EOF
115	Usage: runner.sh --issue <N>|--goal "<text>" [--dry-run] [--template <id>]
116	                 [--resume] [--from-stage <stage>] [--no-resume] [--force]
117	  --issue <N>       GitHub issue number to work
118	  --goal "<text>"   Pipeline goal description (alternative to --issue)
119	  --dry-run         Print the stage plan without executing anything
120	  --template <id>   Pipeline template to use (default: simple)
121	  --resume          Resume an existing run (skip completed stages)
122	  --from-stage <s>  Skip ahead to stage <s> when resuming (emits warning)
123	  --no-resume       Recreate: start fresh even if a state exists and restore no
124	                    prior-run work (default: resume, reusing prior work;
125	                    ZBUILD_RESUME=0 is the same, #2225)
126	  --force           Resume even if status=aborted
127	  --self-host       Dogfood zBuild's own engine: redirect read-only contract-
128	                    grammar libs to a working-tree snapshot (#963, ADR-023)

130	Environment:
131	  ZBUILD_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE  Force a single platform; detection short-circuits.
132	  ZBUILD_SCOPE_PATHS        Newline-delimited scope paths; written as '+ <path>' entries.
133	  ZBUILD_SELF_HOST          Set to 1 to enable self-host mode (same as --self-host).
134	  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR   Override dir contract-reader stages source grammar libs from.

138	# Helpers extracted to dispatch.sh / state_helpers.sh in #279:
139	#   _find_plugin_for_stage       → core/pipeline/dispatch.sh
140	#   write_scope_override
141	#   _update_stage_status         } → core/pipeline/state_helpers.sh
142	#   _set_pipeline_status
143	#   (+ their _zbuild_runner_set_* jq filter helpers)

145	# Globals (not local) so EXIT trap can read them after main() returns.
146	_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""
147	# #1878: last reported snapshot-failure reason, so a static precondition is
148	# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.
149	_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON=""

151	# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
152	# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
153	# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
154	# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
155	# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
156	# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
157	_runner_retry_budget() {
158	    local v=""
159	    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
161	    fi
162	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
163	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
164	    (( v > 5 )) && v=5
165	    printf '%s' "$v"
166	}

168	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
169	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
170	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
171	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
172	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
173	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
174	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
175	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
176	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
177	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
178	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
179	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
180	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
181	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
182	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
183	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
184	    _runner_ended=true
185	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
186	    return 0
187	}

189	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
190	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
191	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
192	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
193	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
194	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
195	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
196	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
197	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
198	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
199	    case "$v" in
200	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
201	        *) return 1 ;;
202	    esac
203	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
204	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
205	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
206	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
207	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
208	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
209	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
210	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
211	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
212	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
213	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
214	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
215	    _runner_ended=true
216	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
217	    return 0
218	}

220	# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
221	# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
222	# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
223	# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
224	# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
225	# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
226	_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
227	    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
228	    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
229	    local latest="" n=0 d k
230	    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
231	        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
232	        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
233	        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
234	        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
235	    done
236	    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
237	    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
238	    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
239	        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
240	        return
241	    fi
242	    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
243	    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
244	}

246	# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
247	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
248	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
249	_runner_note_push_failure() {
250	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
251	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
252	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
253	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
254	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
255	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
256	}

258	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
259	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
260	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
261	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
262	# when HEAD carries commits past the run's baseline — and before intake has
263	# recorded that baseline the run has made none, so nothing is pushed (#1801 run
264	# 38290215955: the end of hydrate force-pushed main over the branch's earlier
265	# work). Advisory: a failure is reported, never fatal.
266	_runner_push_work_branch() {
267	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
268	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
269	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
270	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
271	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
272	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
273	    local _base="" _ahead
274	    [[ -f "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" ]] && _base="$(cat "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" 2>/dev/null || true)"
275	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
276	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
277	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
278	    local _err
279	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
280	        return 0
281	    fi
282	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
283	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
284	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
285	    return 0
286	}

288	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
289	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
290	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
291	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
292	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
293	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
294	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
295	    local _sd="${1:-}" _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch=""
296	    [[ -f "$_sd/intake-branch.txt" ]] && read -r _branch 2>/dev/null < "$_sd/intake-branch.txt"
297	    _branch="${_branch//[[:space:]]/}"
298	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
299	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
300	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
301	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
302	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
303	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
304	        reattached)
305	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
306	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
307	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
308	        diverged)
309	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
310	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
311	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
312	    esac
313	    return 0
314	}

316	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
317	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
318	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
319	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
320	# never blocks a run.
321	#
322	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
323	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
324	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
325	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
326	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
327	# item 1 of #1807.
328	#
329	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
330	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
331	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
332	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
333	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
334	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
335	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
336	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
337	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
338	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
339	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
340	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
341	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
342	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
343	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
344	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
345	    # push had nothing to send.
346	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
347	
348	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
349	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
350	        saved)
351	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
352	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
353	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
354	            ;;
355	        failed)
356	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
357	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
358	            # no channel to surface on.
359	            #
360	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
361	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
362	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
363	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
364	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
365	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
366	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
367	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
368	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
369	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
370	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
371	            fi
372	            ;;
373	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
374	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
375	        *) : ;;
376	    esac
377	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
378	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
379	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
380	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
381	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
382	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
383	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
384	    local _leak=""
385	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
386	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
387	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
388	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
389	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
390	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
391	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
392	        return 0
393	    fi
394	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
395	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
396	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
397	    fi
398	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
399	    return 0
400	}

402	# ─── stage-start time cache (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────
403	# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
404	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
405	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.

408	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
409	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
410	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
411	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
412	# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).

415	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
416	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
417	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
418	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
419	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
420	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
421	_runner_now_ms() {
422	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
423	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
424	        printf '%s' "$ovr"
425	        return 0
426	    fi
427	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
428	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
429	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
430	        return 0
431	    fi
432	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
433	}

435	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
436	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
437	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
438	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
439	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
440	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
441	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
442	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
443	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
444	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
445	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
446	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
447	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
448	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
449	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
450	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
451	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
452	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
453	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
454	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
455	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
456	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
457	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
458	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
459	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
460	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
461	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
462	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
463	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
464	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
465	    return 0
466	}

468	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
469	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
470	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
471	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
472	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
473	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
474	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
475	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
476	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
477	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
478	        local i
479	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
480	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
481	            sleep 0.1
482	        done
483	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
484	    fi
485	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
486	    return 0
487	}

489	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
490	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
491	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
492	_runner_now_short() {
493	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
494	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
495	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
496	        return 0
497	    fi
498	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
499	    local out
500	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
501	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
502	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
503	    printf '%s' "$out"
504	}

506	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
507	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
508	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
509	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
510	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
511	_runner_duration_token() {
512	    local stage="$1"
513	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
514	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
515	        printf '?s'
516	        return 0
517	    fi
518	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
519	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
520	        printf '?s'
521	        return 0
522	    fi
523	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
524	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
525	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
526	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
527	    else
528	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
529	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
530	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
531	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
532	    fi
533	}

569	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
570	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
571	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
572	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
573	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
574	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
575	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
576	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
577	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
578	_runner_record_report() {
579	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
580	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
581	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
582	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
583	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
584	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
585	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
586	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
587	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
588	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
589	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
590	        sleep 0.05
591	    done
592	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
593	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
594	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
595	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
596	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
597	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
598	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
599	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
600	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
601	    else
602	        rm -f "$tmp"
603	    fi
604	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
605	    return 0
606	}

608	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
609	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
610	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
611	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
612	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
613	#
614	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
615	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
616	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
617	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
618	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
619	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
620	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
621	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
622	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
623	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
624	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
625	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
626	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
627	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
628	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
629	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
630	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
631	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
632	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
633	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
634	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
635	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
636	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
637	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
638	        return 1
639	    fi
640	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
641	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
642	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
643	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
644	        return 1
645	    fi
646	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
647	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
648	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
649	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
650	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
651	    #
652	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
653	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
654	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
655	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
656	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
657	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
658	    #
659	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
660	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
661	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
662	    #
663	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
664	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
665	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
666	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
667	    fi
668	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
669	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
670	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
671	    # an unchanged tree.
672	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
673	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
674	    fi
675	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
676	    local _leaf _ok=1
677	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
678	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
679	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
680	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
681	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
682	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
683	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
684	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
685	        esac
686	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
687	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
688	            _ok=0
689	        fi
690	    done
691	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
692	}

694	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
695	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
696	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
697	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
698	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
699	#
700	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
701	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
702	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
703	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
704	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
705	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
706	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
707	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
708	#
709	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
710	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
711	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
712	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
713	#
714	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
715	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
716	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
717	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
718	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
719	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
720	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
721	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
722	_runner_template_personas() {
723	    awk '
724	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
725	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
726	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
727	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
728	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
729	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
730	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
731	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
732	        }
733	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
734	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
735	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
736	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
737	        }
738	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
739	}

741	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
742	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
743	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
744	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
745	    case "$mode" in
746	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
747	        *) mode="warn" ;;
748	    esac
749	
750	    # off = complete no-op, no output
751	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
752	
753	    local -a violations=()
754	    local fail_count=0
755	
756	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
757	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
758	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")
759	        fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
760	    fi
761	
762	    # ADR-051 §2 (amended 2026-10-12): every persona the template names — a
763	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
764	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
765	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.
766	    local _persona_missing=0 _pw _pid _pdir
767	    if [[ -n "${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE" ]]; then
768	        # shellcheck source=/dev/null  # followed, it re-reads runner.sh's own includes
769	        declare -F persona_find_dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
770	            || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
771	        while IFS='|' read -r _pw _pid; do
772	            [[ -n "$_pid" ]] || continue
773	            _pdir="$(persona_find_dir "$_pid" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$_pdir" ]] && continue
774	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")
775	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1)); _persona_missing=1
776	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")
777	    fi

779	    # No violations → clean
780	    [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]] && return 0

782	    # Render all violations in a single block (render-all-at-once pattern).
783	    # #1826 moved the loop itself into _inputs_render_violations so the
784	    # pre-dispatch input presence check reuses it instead of being a third
785	    # aggregation loop; the rendered bytes are unchanged.
786	    _inputs_render_violations \
787	        "Startup preflight: persona bindings or required plugins are unresolvable:" \
788	        "Fix: ensure the declared persona id exists under plugins/persona/<id>/manifest.yaml
789	     and that each requires.plugins entry names an installable plugin.
790	     See docs/adr/ADR-051-engine-owned-stage-keyed-data-provision.md." \
791	        "${violations[@]}"
792	
793	    # Emit event (best-effort)
794	    if declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
795	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.preflight.fail" \
796	            "reason=startup_preflight" \
797	            "violation_count=$fail_count" \
798	            "mode=$mode" 2>/dev/null || true

800	
801	    if [[ "$mode" == "warn" && "$_persona_missing" -eq 0 ]]; then
802	        printf '  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn — continuing despite startup preflight violations. Set =enforce to fail-fast.\n\n' >&2
803	        return 0
804	    fi
805	
806	    # enforce: fail-closed
807	    return 1
808	}

879	        preflight_failed)              verdict_glyph "warn" ;;

898	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
899	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
900	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
901	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
902	#
903	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
904	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
905	#
906	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
907	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
908	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
909	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
910	#
911	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
912	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
913	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
914	# against banner-write failures.
915	_render_pipeline_end() {
916	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
917	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
918	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
919	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
920	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
921	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
922	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
923	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
924	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
925	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
926	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
927	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
928	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
929	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
930	    # (#1156)
931	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
932	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
933	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
934	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
935	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
936	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
937	
938	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
939	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
940	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
941	    local word
942	    case "$status" in
943	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
944	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
945	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
946	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
947	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
948	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
949	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
950	    esac
951	
952	    local label=" pipeline.end "
953	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
954	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
955	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
956	
957	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
958	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
959	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
960	
961	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
962	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
963	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
964	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
965	        local bar
966	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
967	        bar="${bar// /═}"
968	        {
969	            printf '\n'
970	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
971	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
972	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
973	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
974	        } >&2
975	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
976	        return 0
977	    fi
978	
979	    local lbar rbar
980	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
981	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
982	    {
983	        printf '\n'
984	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
985	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
986	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
987	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
988	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
989	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
990	    } >&2
991	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
992	}
993	
994	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not
995	# pass ends by saying why in words and naming each open item, with what would
996	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
997	_runner_render_open_items() {
998	    case "${1:-}" in failed|interrupted|aborted) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
999	    [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]] && declare -F open_items_markdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
1000	    local sd="${_runner_state_file%/*}" items n
1001	    items="$(open_items_markdown "$sd")" || items=""
1002	    n=0; [[ -n "$items" ]] && n="$(grep -c '^[0-9][0-9]*\. ' <<< "$items" || true)"
1003	    {
1004	        printf 'The run %s.\n' "$(run_end_words "${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-}" "$n")"
1005	        [[ -n "$items" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$items"
1006	    } >&2
1007	}
1008	
1009	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1010	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1011	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1012	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1013	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1014	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1015	#
1016	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1017	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1018	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1019	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1020	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1021	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1022	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1023	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1024	_render_stage_divider() {
1025	    local stage="$1"
1026	    local width
1027	    width="$(_term_width)"
1028	    local color
1029	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1030	    local label=" ${stage} "
1031	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1032	
1033	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1034	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1035	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1036	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1037	
1038	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1039	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1040	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1041	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1042	        local bar
1043	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1044	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1045	        {
1046	            printf '\n'
1047	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1048	            printf '\n'
1049	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1050	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1051	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1052	            printf '\n'
1053	        } >&2
1054	        return 0
1055	    fi
1056	
1057	    local lbar rbar
1058	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1059	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1060	    {
1061	        printf '\n'
1062	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1063	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1064	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1065	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1066	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1067	        printf '\n'
1068	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1069	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1070	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1071	        printf '\n'
1072	    } >&2
1073	}
1074	
1075	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1076	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1077	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1078	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1079	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1080	#
1081	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1082	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1083	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1084	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN
1085	#
1086	# Routing contract (silent-failure mitigations):
1087	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)
1088	#     — output would vanish. Banner emit follows event emit (event=durable,
1089	#     banner=best-effort).
1090	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1091	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1092	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1093	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1094	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.
1095	#
1096	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1097	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).
1098	
1099	# ─── _render_cycle_entry <cycle_id> <max> <stages_csv> ───────────────────────
1100	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering cycle <id>` line + DIM trailer
1101	# (max + stages). Emitted by the runner BEFORE cycle_orchestrator_run so the
1102	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.
1103	_render_cycle_entry() {
1104	    local cycle_id="$1" max="$2" stages_csv="${3:-}" description="${4:-}"
1105	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1106	    local label=" cycle: ${cycle_id} "
1107	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1108	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1109	    local bar
1110	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1111	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1112	    {
1113	        printf '\n'
1114	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1115	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1116	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1117	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1118	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1119	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$cycle_id" "${RESET:-}"
1120	        # #831: operator-facing description on its own DIM line, between the
1121	        # Entering-cycle headline and the (max_iterations=…) trailer. Skipped
1122	        # entirely when description is empty so templates without it render
1123	        # identically to the pre-#831 banner (golden tests stay valid).
1124	        if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
1125	            printf '%b  %s%b\n' "${DIM:-}" "$description" "${RESET:-}"
1126	        fi
1127	        printf '%b  (max_iterations=%s · stages=%s)%b\n' \
1128	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$stages_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1129	        printf '\n'
1130	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1131	}
1132	
1133	# ─── _render_parallel_entry <group_id> <max_parallel> <members_csv> ──────────
1134	# ADR-039 (#1131): clone of _render_cycle_entry for a parallel stage group.
1135	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering parallel group <id>` line + DIM
1136	# trailer (max_parallel + members). Emitted by the runner BEFORE
1137	# parallel_group_run so the operator's eye finds the group boundary first.
1138	_render_parallel_entry() {
1139	    local group_id="$1" max="$2" members_csv="${3:-}"
1140	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1141	    local label=" parallel: ${group_id} "
1142	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1143	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1144	    local bar
1145	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1146	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1147	    {
1148	        printf '\n'
1149	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1150	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1151	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1152	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering parallel group: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1153	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1154	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$group_id" "${RESET:-}"
1155	        printf '%b  (max_parallel=%s · members=%s)%b\n' \
1156	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$members_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1157	        printf '\n'
1158	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1159	}
1160	
1161	# ─── _render_parallel_group_complete <group_id> <member_count> <failure_count> ─
1162	# Issue OUT (ADR-039): DIM trailer after a parallel group's per-member lines,
1163	# mirroring _render_cycle_exit's role for cycles. e.g.
1164	# `▸ review_lenses complete — 5 members, 0 blocking`.
1165	_render_parallel_group_complete() {
1166	    local group_id="$1" count="${2:-0}" fail="${3:-0}"
1167	    {
1168	        printf '%b▸ %s complete — %s members, %s blocking%b\n' \
1169	            "${DIM:-}" "$group_id" "$count" "$fail" "${RESET:-}"
1170	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1171	}
1172	
1173	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_divider <cycle_id> <iter> <max> ───────────────────────
1174	# Light `─` CYAN sub-divider for each iter boundary, e.g.
1175	# `─── build_test_cycle iter 2/5 ─────`. When this cycle is nested inside
1176	# another cycle the orchestrator has already set ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX (e.g.
1177	# `4.1`) — surface it as a `[<prefix>]` prefix so operators can tell at a
1178	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1179	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1180	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1181	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1182	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1183	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1184	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1185	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1186	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1187	    local label
1188	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1189	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1190	    else
1191	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1192	    fi
1193	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1194	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1195	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1196	    local bar
1197	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1198	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1199	    {
1200	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1201	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1202	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1203	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1204	}
1205	
1206	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1207	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1208	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1209	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1210	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1211	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1212	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1213	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1214	    {
1215	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1216	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1217	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1218	}
1219	
1220	# ─── _render_cycle_exit <cycle_id> <reason> <iter> <max> ──────────────────────
1221	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + verdict-glyph line mapping termination reason
1222	# to glyph + color (see #524 spec).
1223	#   converged       → ✓ GREEN+BOLD
1224	#   max_iterations  → ✗ RED+BOLD
1225	#   plateau         → ✗ RED+BOLD
1226	#   divergence      → ✗ RED+BOLD
1227	#   aborted         → ⚠ YELLOW+BOLD
