1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/orch/local_engine.sh — shared dispatch/collect/poll/shutdown for the
3	# local-execution orchestrator backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive).
4	# Extracted from those two plugins in #281 because they had ~80% duplication
5	# and the #269 normaliser fix had to be applied twice (and still missed
6	# orch-mock — caught belatedly in #278). Single source of truth now.
7	#
8	# Pool layout (caller chooses prefix + pid subdir name):
9	#   <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/<slot>.pid       — wrapper subshell PID
10	#   <pool_dir>/results/<slot>.{stdout,stderr,exit,inner_pid}
11	#
12	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; no set -euo pipefail.
13	
14	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
15	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED=1
16	
17	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
18	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
19	
20	# Defensive source: warn (scripts/lib/helpers.sh).
21	if ! declare -F warn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
22	    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
23	fi
24	
25	# Load process-group kill helpers (zbuild_pg_kill, zbuild_pid_kill).
26	if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
28	fi
29	
30	# _orch_local_make_slot_id — collision-resistant slot id (epoch-ns + PID + rand)
31	_orch_local_make_slot_id() {
32	    date +%s%N
33	    printf -- '-%s-' "$$"
34	    openssl rand -hex 8 2>/dev/null || printf '%05d%05d%05d' $RANDOM $RANDOM $RANDOM
35	}
36	
37	
38	# _orch_local_dispatch_workunit <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <work_unit> <caller_tag>
39	# Dispatches <work_unit> (must be an executable file path) in a background
40	# subshell. Records wrapper PID and inner PID; installs trap to propagate
41	# SIGTERM/EXIT to the inner process.
42	#
43	# Output: prints slot_id to stdout AND sets the global _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID.
44	# Callers needing the slot_id after dispatch (e.g. for downstream telemetry)
45	# MUST read the global, NOT use command substitution: `$(_orch_local_dispatch_workunit ...)`
46	# forks a subshell whose EXIT trap (installed by test-helpers.sh or similar)
47	# `pkill -P $$`s the wrapper subshell we just spawned. The global pattern
48	# avoids that subshell entirely. (Caught in #282 second-round review.)
49	#
50	# Returns 0 on successful dispatch, 1 on validation/permission failure.
51	_orch_local_dispatch_workunit() {
52	    local pool_dir="$1"
53	    local pid_subdir="$2"
54	    local work_unit="$3"
55	    local caller_tag="${4:-orch_local}"
56	
57	    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID=""
58	
59	    if [[ ! -f "$work_unit" || ! -x "$work_unit" ]]; then
60	        warn "${caller_tag}: work_unit must be a path to an executable file: ${work_unit}" || true
61	        return 1
62	    fi
63	
64	    # Ensure pool dirs exist even if the caller skipped pre-spawn.
65	    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results" "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" 2>/dev/null || {
66	        warn "${caller_tag}: pool dir is not writable: ${pool_dir}" || true
67	        return 1
68	    }
69	
70	    local slot_id
71	    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
72	    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
73	
74	    # Background subshell: writes inner work-unit PID, traps on exit to
75	    # propagate signals, then waits for inner and writes .exit file.
76	    (
77	        local rc=0 inner=0
78	        # #2108: dispatched from a `<<< "$roles_out"` loop — never its stdin.
79	        bash "$work_unit" </dev/null > "${result_base}.stdout" 2> "${result_base}.stderr" &
80	        inner=$!
81	        echo "$inner" > "${result_base}.inner_pid"
82	        trap 'kill -KILL "$inner" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT INT TERM
83	        wait "$inner" || rc=$?
84	        trap - EXIT INT TERM
85	        echo "$rc" > "${result_base}.exit"
86	    ) &
87	    local worker_pid=$!
88	    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
89	    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
90	    echo "$slot_id"
91	    return 0
92	}
93	
94	# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
95	# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
96	# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
97	#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
98	#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
99	#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
100	#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
101	# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
102	# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
103	_orch_local_collect_results() {
104	    local pool_dir="$1"
105	    local pid_subdir="$2"
106	    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
107	    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
108	
109	    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }
110	
111	    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
112	    local deadline=0
113	    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))
114	
115	    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
116	    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
117	        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
118	        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
119	        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
120	        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
121	        inner_pid=""
122	        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"
123	
124	        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
125	            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
126	                if declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
127	                    zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
128	                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
129	                else
130	                    kill -TERM "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
131	                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill -TERM "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
132	                fi
133	                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
134	                break
135	            fi
136	            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
137	        done
138	
139	        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
140	        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
141	        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
142	        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
143	            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
144	        else
145	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
146	        fi
147	    done
148	
149	    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
150	        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
151	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
152	        return 0
153	    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
154	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
155	        return 1
156	    else
157	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	}
161	
162	# _orch_local_shutdown_pool <pool_dir> <pid_subdir>
163	# Best-effort SIGTERM → 0.5s → SIGKILL on every slot, then rm -rf the pool dir.
164	# Idempotent — safe to call on non-existent pools.
165	_orch_local_shutdown_pool() {
166	    local pool_dir="$1"
167	    local pid_subdir="$2"
168	
169	    [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]] || return 0
170	
171	    local pid_file slot_id wrapper_pid inner_pid
172	    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
173	        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
174	        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
175	        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
176	        inner_pid=""
177	        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
178	            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
179	        if declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
180	            zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
181	            [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
182	        else
183	            kill -TERM "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
184	            [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill -TERM "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
185	        fi
186	    done
187	    rm -rf "$pool_dir"
188	    return 0
189	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1
9	
10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}
74	
75	# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
76	# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}
82	
83	# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
84	#
85	# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
86	# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
92	#
93	# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
94	# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
95	zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
96	    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
97	    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
98	    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
99	    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
100	    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
101	}
102	
103	# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
104	#
105	# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
106	# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
107	# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
108	# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
109	# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
110	# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
111	#
112	# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
113	# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
114	#
115	# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
116	# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
117	# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
118	# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
119	#
120	# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
121	# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
122	zbuild_pg_register() {
123	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
124	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
125	    local _self
126	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
127	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
128	    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
129	    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
130	    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
131	    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
132	    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
133	    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
134	    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
135	    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
136	    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
137	    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
138	    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
139	    local _start
140	    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
141	    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
142	    return 0
143	}
144	
145	# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
146	zbuild_pg_kill() {
147	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
148	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
149	    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
150	    local _self
151	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
152	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
153	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
154	}
155	
156	# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
157	# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
158	# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
159	zbuild_pid_kill() {
160	    local _pid="${1:-}"
161	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
162	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
163	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
18	# the process group would.
19	#
20	# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
21	# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
25	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
26	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
27

108	        # Spawn a child that ignores TERM and records its PID — used to verify

110	        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${BUILD_STARTED%/*}/run-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &

131	        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
132	        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &

139	test_run() {
140	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
141	    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"pass","disposition":"complete","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"

143	}
144	test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
145	PLUG
146	
147	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
148	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
149	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
150	mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
151	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
152	
153	_case_no=0
154	# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
155	_prep() {
156	    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
157	    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
158	    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
159	    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
160	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
161	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
162	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="$CASE_DIR/events/events.db"
163	    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
164	    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
165	    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
166	    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
167	}
168	
169	# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
170	#
171	# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
172	# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
173	# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
174	# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
175	# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
176	# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
177	#
178	# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
179	# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
180	#
181	# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
182	# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
183	# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
184	# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
185	# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
186	# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
187	# returns, which a killed stage never does.
188	_assert_released() {
189	    local _case="$1"; shift
190	    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
191	    local _stage _missing=""
192	    for _stage in "$@"; do
193	        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
194	    done
195	    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
196	        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
197	    else
198	        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
199	            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
200	    fi
201	    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
202	        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
203	    else
204	        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
205	    fi
206	}
207	
208	# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
209	print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
210	_prep success
211	export BUILD_RC=0
212	set +e
213	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
214	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
215	_rc=$?
216	set -e
217	assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
218	_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test
219	
220	# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
221	print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
222	_prep nonzero
223	export BUILD_RC=1
224	set +e
225	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
226	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
227	_rc=$?
228	set -e
229	if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
230	    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
231	else
232	    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
233	fi
234	_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build
235	
236	# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
237	print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
238	_prep sigint
239	export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
240	set +e
241	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
242	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
243	_rc=$?
244	set -e
245	# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
246	# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
247	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
248	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
249	    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
250	_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build
251	
252	# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
253	print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
254	_prep sigterm
255	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
256	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
257	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
258	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
259	    RUNNER_PID=$!
260	else
261	    set -m
262	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
263	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
264	    RUNNER_PID=$!
265	    set +m
266	fi
267	for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
268	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
269	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
270	# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
271	# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
272	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
273	_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build
274	
275	# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
276	# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
277	#
278	# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
279	# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
280	# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
281	# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
282	# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
283	# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
284	# runs could never reproduce.
285	#
286	# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
287	# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
288	# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
289	# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
290	# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
291	print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
292	_prep timeout
293	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
294	_tbin=""
295	if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
296	elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
297	fi
298	if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
299	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
300	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
301	else
302	    # #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own teardown
303	    # budget, not guessed.
304	    #
305	    # The engine bounds each always-run stage by its template `stage_timeout_s`,
306	    # falling back to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30s) only when the template
307	    # sets none (#2287) — so the pin below is a fallback, and this case relies on
308	    # its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound. Three stages
309	    # release on this path, so an unpinned run is entitled to spend far longer
310	    # tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here. When it did, this
311	    # test SIGKILLed the runner mid-teardown and then asserted on the markers
312	    # teardown had not yet written: the marker came back EMPTY, with BOTH stages
313	    # missing rather than one. Under a loaded machine that is exactly what
314	    # happened, intermittently, for as long as this test has existed.
315	    #
316	    # Pin the budget so the worst case is knowable, then clear it with margin.
317	    # The backstop exists so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite —
318	    # it must never be the thing that stops teardown finishing.
319	    _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=3
320	    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
321	    set -m
322	    ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S="$_SPEC5_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
323	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
324	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
325	    RUNNER_PID=$!
326	    set +m
327	    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -f "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
328	    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
329	    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
330	    _spec5_killer=$!
331	    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
332	    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
333	    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
334	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
335	    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
336	fi
337	
338	# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
339	# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
340	# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
341	# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
342	print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
343	_prep blocking
344	export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP=1
345	_t0=$(date +%s)
346	set +e
347	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-blocking" ) \
348	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
349	set -e
350	_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
351	unset BLOCK_CLEANUP
352	# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
353	# `stage_timeout_s` (30 in the template, which takes precedence over
354	# ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S), so the runner returns in about 30s. Allow generous
355	# headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
356	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
357	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
358	else
359	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
360	fi
361	# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
362	# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
363	# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
364	# runner returns; the 1s grace only covers the killed processes exiting on a
365	# loaded host.
366	sleep 1
367	_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
368	if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
369	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
370	elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
371	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
372	    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
373	    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
374	    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
375	    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
376	    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
377	else
378	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
379	fi
380	
381	# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
382	# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
383	# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
384	# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
385	print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
386	# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
387	# case is only about what survives it.
388	_prep blocking-ignore-term
389	export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM=1
390	set +e
391	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-ignore-term" ) \
392	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
393	set -e
394	unset BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM
395	_child_pid=""
396	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
397	    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
398	    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
399	done
400	_alive=1
401	# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
402	if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
403	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
404	fi
405	if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
406	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
407	elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
408	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
409	    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
410	else
411	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
412	fi
413	
414	# ── SPEC-2ext [#1801/SPEC-2]: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group
415	# SPEC-2 says: "when the runner is externally killed, its signal handler must
416	# also kill any isolated hook process group". The run hook spawns a child that
417	# ignores TERM. After the runner is externally killed, the child must not survive
418	# because zbuild_pg_kill (or the equivalent KILL sequence) sends SIGKILL to the
419	# entire process group, which the child cannot ignore.
420	print_test_section "SPEC-2ext: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group [#1801/SPEC-2]"
421	_prep sigterm-runpg
422	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM=1
423	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
424	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
425	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
426	    RUNNER_PID=$!
427	else
428	    set -m
429	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
430	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
431	    RUNNER_PID=$!
432	    set +m
433	fi
434	_run_child_pid=""
435	for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
436	    _run_child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/run-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
437	    [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
438	done
439	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
440	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
441	unset BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM
442	_alive_run=1
443	if [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
444	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive_run=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
445	fi
446	if [[ -z "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
447	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] fixture: run hook child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/run-child.pid"
448	elif [[ "$_alive_run" -eq 1 ]]; then
449	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)" \
450	        "pid $_run_child_pid still alive — hook process group was not killed when runner received SIGTERM"
451	    kill -KILL "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
452	else
453	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)"
454	fi
455	
456	cleanup_test_env
457	print_test_results
458	exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (Wave 15-H / #688): flag-gated process-group signal
3	# forwarding via bash job control in the runner.
4	#
5	# When ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1:
6	#   - the runner enables `set -m` at startup;
7	#   - the SIGINT/TERM trap walks `jobs -p` and TERM-then-KILL's each
8	#     child PGID, reaping whole subtrees.
9	#
10	# Discriminating assertions:
11	#   (T1) With flag on, the runner shell has `monitor` (-m) option set —
12	#        verified by injecting a probe plugin that records `$-` and
13	#        `set -o monitor` output. Flag-off: no `-m`.
14	#   (T2) With flag on, SIGTERM mid-build still produces exit 1 + the
15	#        Wave 15-B sentinel/event chain (regression of trap composition) —
16	#        the signal is named by pipeline.aborted reason=sigterm (#1850,
17	#        ADR-054 §4: the exit status was 143).
18	#
19	# Wave 15-H lays the foundation for future backgrounded stages (e.g.
20	# parallel strategy fanout); the trap's PG-kill loop is exercised here
21	# transitively by T2's end-to-end SIGTERM. The current dispatch path
22	# runs plugins in foreground subshells (no `&`), so a flag-on test that
23	# requires a backgrounded runner-child would not reflect realistic usage
24	# and is intentionally omitted.
25	#
26	set -euo pipefail
27	
28	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
29	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
30	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
31	
32	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
33	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
34	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
35	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
36	
37	print_test_header "runner job-control PG forwarding (Wave 15-H / #688)"
38	setup_test_env "runner-job-control-abort"
39	
40	_test_cleanup_hook() {
41	    if [[ "${KEEP_TMP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
42	        echo "KEEPTEMP=$TEST_TEMP_DIR" >&2
43	    else
44	        cleanup_test_env
45	    fi
46	}
47	
48	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
49	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
50	mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
51	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
52	
53	# ─── T1: flag toggles `-m` (monitor mode) on the runner shell ────────────────
54	print_test_section "T1: ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1 enables set -m in runner"
55	
56	PROBE_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-probe"
57	PROBE_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"   # mock_plugin_factory uses TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins
58	PROBE_EVENTS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-probe/events.jsonl"
59	mkdir -p "$PROBE_STATE_DIR" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-probe"
60	PROBE_OPTS_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/intake-shell-opts"
61	
62	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PROBE_PLUGINS"
63	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$PROBE_STATE_DIR"
64	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-probe"
65	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$PROBE_EVENTS"
66	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
67	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
68	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
69	
70	# #978: job-control PG forwarding is roster-agnostic — T1 probes the runner
71	# shell's monitor-mode via intake, and T2 signals mid-build and asserts test
72	# never runs. Drive a MINIMAL 3-leaf fixture (intake → build → test) instead of
73	# pinning to the standard roster (retired in #979). #1270: install the fixture as
74	# a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay in a temp repo and run with CWD = that
75	# repo (the resolver reads the overlay from $PWD). intake/build/test get custom
76	# bodies below.
77	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo tpl-overlay-repo)"
78	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
79	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
80	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
81	mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null
82	
83	# Probe intake records $- (set of shell option flags) to a marker so we
84	# can introspect whether the runner shell has 'm' (monitor mode) set.
85	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PROBE
86	intake_run() {
87	    echo "dash=\$-" > "${PROBE_OPTS_FILE}"
88	    set -o | grep -E '^monitor' >> "${PROBE_OPTS_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || true
89	    $(mock_v2_result_line intake)
90	    return 0
91	}
92	PROBE
93	
94	# Run with flag OFF.
95	: > "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE"
96	unset ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL
97	rm -f "$PROBE_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
98	set +e
99	# #1270: CWD = overlay repo so the resolver finds the resume-minimal fixture.
100	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "w15h probe flag-off" ) \
101	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-off.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-off.stderr"
102	rc_off=$?
103	set -e
104	opts_off="$(cat "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
105	
106	# Run with flag ON.
107	: > "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE"
108	export ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1
109	rm -f "$PROBE_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
110	set +e
111	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "w15h probe flag-on" ) \
112	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-on.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-on.stderr"
113	rc_on=$?
114	set -e
115	opts_on="$(cat "$PROBE_OPTS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
116	
117	# Both runs must exit 0.
118	assert_eq "flag-off probe run rc=0" "0" "$rc_off"
119	assert_eq "flag-on  probe run rc=0" "0" "$rc_on"
120	# #2193: a probe that exits non-zero must say why — CI showed only "got: 1".
121	for _pr in off on; do
122	    _rcv="rc_$_pr"
123	    if [[ "${!_rcv}" != "0" ]]; then
124	        echo "--- runner-$_pr.stderr (tail) ---" >&2
125	        tail -30 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-$_pr.stderr" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
126	    fi
127	done
128	
129	# Flag-off: $- must NOT contain 'm'; set -o monitor must be off.
130	if grep -qE 'dash=[^m]*$|dash=[^m]*[^m]*$' <<< "$opts_off" && \
131	   grep -qE '^monitor[[:space:]]+off$' <<< "$opts_off"; then
132	    assert_pass "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell"
133	else
134	    # Looser check: dash line should not have 'm'.
135	    _opts_off_1="$(head -1 <<< "$opts_off")"
136	    if grep -qv 'm' <<< "$_opts_off_1"; then
137	        assert_pass "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell (dash check)"
138	    else
139	        assert_fail "flag-off: monitor mode OFF in runner shell" \
140	            "got: $opts_off"
141	    fi
142	fi
143	
144	# Flag-on: $- must contain 'm' OR set -o monitor must be on.
145	_opts_on_1="$(head -1 <<< "$opts_on")"
146	if grep -q 'm' <<< "$_opts_on_1" || \
147	   grep -qE '^monitor[[:space:]]+on$' <<< "$opts_on"; then
148	    assert_pass "flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell"
149	else
150	    assert_fail "flag-on: monitor mode ON in runner shell" \
151	        "got: $opts_on"
152	fi
153	
154	# ─── T2: SIGTERM with flag-on still produces exit 1 + Wave 15-B chain ────────
155	print_test_section "T2: end-to-end SIGTERM with flag-on (regression of trap chain)"
156	
157	# Reuse $PROBE_PLUGINS (= TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins). Override build/test/intake.
158	E2E_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-e2e"
159	E2E_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e/events.jsonl"
160	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$E2E_STATE_DIR"
161	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e"
162	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$E2E_EVENTS_JSONL"
163	mkdir -p "$E2E_STATE_DIR" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-e2e"
164	export ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1
165	
166	E2E_BUILD_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-build-started"
167	E2E_TEST_RAN="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-test-ran"
168	export E2E_BUILD_STARTED E2E_TEST_RAN
169	
170	# Restore intake to a no-op (was overridden by probe).
171	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
172	intake_run() { $(mock_v2_result_line intake); return 0; }
173	PLUG
174	
175	# Build plugin: short polling loop so the trap can fire within budget.
176	# Note: under flag-on, `set -m` puts the plugin subshell in its own PGID
177	# so a kernel-pgrp TERM to the runner does NOT reach the subshell directly.
178	# The runner's trap therefore fires only after the foreground subshell
179	# returns naturally — bounded by the loop length here.
180	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
181	build_run() {
182	    : > "${E2E_BUILD_STARTED}"
183	    local _i
184	    for _i in \$(seq 1 30); do
185	        sleep 0.1
186	    done
187	    $(mock_v2_result_line build)
188	    return 0
189	}
190	PLUG
191	cat > "$PROBE_PLUGINS/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
192	test_run() { : > "${E2E_TEST_RAN}"; $(mock_v2_result_line test); return 0; }
193	PLUG
194	
195	# #1270: the runner resolves the fixture from $PWD, so cd into the overlay repo
196	# before exec-ing it. `exec` replaces the wrapper shell so $! is the runner PID.
197	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
198	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
199	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "w15h e2e" \
200	        >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stderr" &
201	    RUNNER_PID=$!
202	    RUNNER_PGID="$RUNNER_PID"
203	else
204	    set -m
205	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
206	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "w15h e2e" \
207	        >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stderr" &
208	    RUNNER_PID=$!
209	    RUNNER_PGID="$(ps -o pgid= "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo "$RUNNER_PID")"
210	    set +m
211	fi
212	
213	for _ in $(seq 1 600); do
214	    [[ -f "$E2E_BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break
215	    sleep 0.1
216	done
217	if [[ ! -f "$E2E_BUILD_STARTED" ]]; then
218	    kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
219	    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
220	    assert_fail "build stage reached before signal (T2)" \
221	        "stderr tail: $(tail -c 600 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stderr" 2>/dev/null)"
222	    print_test_results
223	    exit 1
224	fi
225	
226	sig_ts=$(date +%s)
227	kill -TERM "-$RUNNER_PGID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
228	
229	set +e
230	wait "$RUNNER_PID"
231	runner_rc=$?
232	set -e
233	end_ts=$(date +%s)
234	sig_to_exit=$(( end_ts - sig_ts ))
235	
236	# #1850: was 143. Every halt exits 1; the word below says it was SIGTERM.
237	assert_eq "runner exits 1, not 143 (flag-on, SIGTERM)" "1" "$runner_rc"
238	assert_eq "pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigterm exactly" "sigterm" \
239	    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$E2E_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
240	
241	# Budget: hang-backstop only (#1059). The abort proof is the exit 1 + reason +
242	# TEST_RAN-absence assertions; this generous bound just catches a true hang
243	# (was a tight ≤5s that flaked on the macOS matrix).
244	if [[ "$sig_to_exit" -le 60 ]]; then
245	    assert_pass "signal-to-exit ≤60s (actual=${sig_to_exit}s)"
246	else
247	    assert_fail "signal-to-exit ≤60s" "actual=${sig_to_exit}s"
248	fi
249	
250	if [[ -f "$E2E_TEST_RAN" ]]; then
251	    assert_fail "test stage did NOT run after SIGTERM" "TEST_RAN sentinel exists"
252	else
253	    assert_pass "test stage did NOT run after SIGTERM"
254	fi
255	
256	e2e_state_file="$E2E_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
257	if [[ -f "$e2e_state_file" ]]; then
258	    status="$(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$e2e_state_file" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
259	    assert_eq "status=interrupted" "interrupted" "$status"
260	else
261	    assert_fail "pipeline-state.json exists" "missing: $e2e_state_file"
262	fi
263	
264	if grep -q '"type":"pipeline.aborted".*sigterm' "$E2E_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null; then
265	    assert_pass "pipeline.aborted reason=sigterm emitted"
266	else
267	    assert_fail "pipeline.aborted reason=sigterm emitted" \
268	        "events tail: $(tail -c 800 "$E2E_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null)"
269	fi
270	
271	# No errors from the new job-control code path.
272	if grep -qiE "set -m: error|jobs -p: error|_runner_signal_trap.*error" \
273	       "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stderr" 2>/dev/null; then
274	    assert_fail "no job-control errors in stderr" \
275	        "stderr tail: $(tail -c 600 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/runner-e2e.stderr")"
276	else
277	    assert_pass "no job-control errors in stderr"
278	fi
279	
280	print_test_results
281	exit $((FAIL > 0))
282

content.content:
1	id: simple
2	name: Simple Pipeline
3	extends: null
4	
5	# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
6	merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged
7	
8	defaults:
9	  strategy: map
10	
11	# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12	# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
13	# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
14	# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
15	# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
16	#
17	# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
18	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
19	# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
20	# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
21	# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
22	# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
23	#
24	# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
25	# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
26	# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
27	# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
28	# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
29	# one work unit per lens element — followed by
30	# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
31	# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
32	# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
33	# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
34	flow:
35	  - hydrate
36	  - intake
37	  - plan
38	  - delivery_loop
39	  - review_lenses
40	  - review-aggregator
41	  - pr
42	
43	# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
45	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
46	#
47	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
48	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
49	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
50	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
51	# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
52	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
53	# called.
54	#
55	# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
56	# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
57	# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
58	#
59	# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
60	# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
61	# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
62	# quietly running nothing.
63	always_run:
64	  - release
65	  - persist
66	
67	# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
68	# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
69	# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
70	# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
71	#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
72	#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
73	delivery_loop:
74	  type: cycle
75	  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
76	  flow:
77	    - design_verify_cycle
78	    - build_test_cycle
79	  exit_when:
80	    all:
81	      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
82	      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
83	  max_iterations: 2
84	  on_max: halt
85	
86	# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
87	# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
88	# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
89	# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
90	# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
91	#
92	# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
93	# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
94	# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
95	# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
96	# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
97	# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
98	# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
99	# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
100	# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
101	#
102	# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
103	# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
104	#
105	design_verify_cycle:
106	  type: cycle
107	  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
108	  flow:
109	    - design
110	    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
111	    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
112	    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
113	    # on the next iteration.
114	    - spec-coverage
115	    - design-gate
116	  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
117	  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
118	  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
119	  # actually cover it.
120	  #
121	  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
122	  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
123	  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
124	  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
125	  exit_when:
126	    all:
127	      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
128	      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
129	  max_iterations: 2
130	  on_max: halt
131	
132	# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
133	# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
134	# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
135	# party cannot re-author it.
136	spec-coverage:
137	  gate: auto
138	  roles: [spec_coverage]
139	  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
140	  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
141	  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
142	  persona: product-owner
143	  stage_timeout_s: 600
144	  router:
145	    timeout_s: 600
146	
147	# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
148	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
149	# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
150	# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
151	test-author:
152	  gate: auto
153	  roles: [test_author]
154	  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
155	  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
156	  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
157	  blocking: true
158	  stage_timeout_s: 900
159	  router:
160	    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
161	    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
162	    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
163	    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
164	    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
165	    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
166	    timeout_s: 900
167	    max_turns: 0
168	    max_iterations: 4
169	
170	# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
171	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
172	# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
173	spec-correspondence:
174	  gate: auto
175	  roles: [spec_correspondence]
176	  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
177	  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
178	  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
179	  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
180	  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
181	  persona: quality-assurance
182	  stage_timeout_s: 600
183	  router:
184	    timeout_s: 600
185	
186	# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
187	# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
188	assertion-integrity:
189	  gate: auto
190	  roles: [assertion_integrity]
191	  stage_timeout_s: 600
192	
193	# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
194	# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
195	# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
196	# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
197	issue-acceptance:
198	  gate: auto
199	  roles: [issue_acceptance]
200	  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
201	  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
202	  persona: product-owner
203	  stage_timeout_s: 600
204	  router:
205	    timeout_s: 600
206	
207	# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
208	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
209	# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
210	# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
211	# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
212	# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
213	# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
214	# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
215	# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
216	# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
217	# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
218	# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
219	# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
220	# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
221	# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
222	# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
223	# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
224	# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
225	# which goes round from design.
226	build_test_cycle:
227	  type: cycle
228	  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
229	  flow:
230	    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
231	    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
232	    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
233	    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
234	    - test-author
235	    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
236	    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
237	    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
238	    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
239	    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
240	    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
241	    - spec-correspondence
242	    - build
243	    - test
244	    - shape-floor
245	    - acceptance-gate
246	    - secret-scan
247	    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
248	    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
249	    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
250	    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
251	    # rewritten assertion.
252	    - assertion-integrity
253	    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
254	    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
255	    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
256	    # requirement is a numbered finding.
257	    - issue-acceptance
258	    - gate-aggregator
259	  exit_when:
260	    stage: gate-aggregator
261	    field: verdict
262	    op: eq
263	    value: pass
264	  max_iterations: 3
265	  on_max: continue
266	  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
267	  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
268	  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
269	  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
270	  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
271	  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
272	  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
273	# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
274	intake:
275	  gate: auto
276	  roles: [intake]
277	  stage_timeout_s: 600
278	  io:
279	    destinations: [file, stdout]
280	    tail_lines: 200
281	
282	# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
283	plan:
284	  gate: auto
285	  roles: [planner]
286	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
287	  persona: product-owner
288	  stage_timeout_s: 1200
289	  io:
290	    destinations: [file, stdout]
291	    tail_lines: 200
292	  router:
293	    timeout_s: 300
294	    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
295	    # headroom. The planner is
296	    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
297	    max_turns: 45
298	
299	# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
300	design:
301	  gate: auto
302	  roles: [designer]
303	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
304	  persona: architect
305	  stage_timeout_s: 3900
306	  io:
307	    destinations: [file, stdout]
308	    tail_lines: 200
309	  router:
310	    timeout_s: 600
311	    max_turns: 0
312	
313	# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
314	# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
315	# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
316	# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
317	# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
318	# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
319	# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
320	# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
321	design-gate:
322	  gate: auto
323	  roles: [design_gate]
324	  stage_timeout_s: 600
325	  io:
326	    destinations: [file, stdout]
327	    tail_lines: 200
328	
329	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
330	build:
331	  gate: auto
332	  roles: [builder]
333	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
334	  persona: developer
335	  stage_timeout_s: 4200
336	  io:
337	    destinations: [file, stdout]
338	    tail_lines: 200
339	  router:
340	    timeout_s: 900
341	    max_turns: 0
342	
343	# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
344	test:
345	  gate: auto
346	  roles: [tester]
347	  stage_timeout_s: 5400
348	  io:
349	    destinations: [file, stdout]
350	    tail_lines: 200
351	
352	# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
353	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
354	shape-floor:
355	  gate: auto
356	  roles: [shape_floor]
357	  stage_timeout_s: 600
358	  io:
359	    destinations: [file, stdout]
360	    tail_lines: 200
361	
362	# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
363	# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
364	# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
365	# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
366	# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
367	# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
368	# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
369	# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
370	acceptance-gate:
371	  gate: auto
372	  roles: [acceptance_gate]
373	  negctl_timeout_s: 60
374	  stage_timeout_s: 600
375	  io:
376	    destinations: [file, stdout]
377	    tail_lines: 200
378	  router:
379	    timeout_s: 600
380	    max_turns: 10
381	
382	# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
383	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
384	# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
385	secret-scan:
386	  gate: auto
387	  roles: [secret_scan]
388	  stage_timeout_s: 600
389	  io:
390	    destinations: [file, stdout]
391	    tail_lines: 200
392	
393	# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
394	# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
395	# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
396	# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
397	gate-aggregator:
398	  gate: auto
399	  roles: [gate_aggregator]
400	  stage_timeout_s: 600
401	  io:
402	    destinations: [file, stdout]
403	    tail_lines: 200
404	
405	# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
406	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
407	# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
408	# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
409	# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
410	# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
411	# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
412	# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
413	# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
414	#
415	# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
416	# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
417	# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
418	review_lenses:
419	  type: map
420	  over: lenses
421	  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
422	  # from the lens's name.
423	  elements:
424	    - id: security
425	      persona: security
426	    - id: performance
427	      persona: performance
428	    - id: red-team
429	      persona: red-team
430	    - id: correctness
431	      persona: correctness
432	    - id: scope
433	      persona: scope
434	    - id: sre
435	      persona: sre
436	  roles: [review_lens]
437	  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
438	  max_parallel: 4
439	  on_member_error: continue
440	  aggregate: advisory
441	  stage_timeout_s: 600
442	  io:
443	    destinations: [file]
444	    tail_lines: 200
445	  router:
446	    timeout_s: 300
447	    max_turns: 25
448	
449	# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
450	# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
451	# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
452	# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
453	# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
454	# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
455	# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
456	# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
457	# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
458	review-aggregator:
459	  gate: auto
460	  roles: [review_aggregator]
461	  stage_timeout_s: 600
462	  io:
463	    destinations: [file, stdout]
464	    tail_lines: 200
465	
466	# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
467	# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
468	pr:
469	  gate: auto
470	  roles: [pr]
471	  stage_timeout_s: 600
472	  io:
473	    destinations: [file, stdout]
474	    tail_lines: 200
475	
476	# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
477	# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
478	# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
479	# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
480	# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
481	#
482	# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
483	# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
484	# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
485	release:
486	  gate: auto
487	  roles: [teardown]
488	  stage_timeout_s: 30
489	  io:
490	    destinations: [file]
491	    tail_lines: 50
492	
493	# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
494	# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
495	# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
496	# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
497	# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
498	# abort.
499	#
500	# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
501	# process-group kill does not.
502	persist:
503	  gate: auto
504	  roles: [persist]
505	  stage_timeout_s: 120
506	  io:
507	    destinations: [file]
508	    tail_lines: 50
509	
510	# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
511	# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
512	# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
513	# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
514	#
515	# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
516	# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
517	# an earlier push never delivered.
518	hydrate:
519	  gate: auto
520	  roles: [hydrate]
521	  stage_timeout_s: 600
522	  router:
523	    timeout_s: 60
524	  io:
525	    destinations: [file]
526	    tail_lines: 50

Integration test for `#1829`/`ADR-054 §7`. Asserts cleanup(`release`) is dispatched on every runner exit path:
- **SPEC-1**: success (rc 0) — all three stages (intake, build, test) release

Integration test for Wave 15-H / `#688`. Asserts flag-gated process-group signal forwarding via bash job control:

- **always_run**: `release`, then `persist` (run on every exit path — success, failure, SIGINT, SIGTERM, timeout)

- **review_lenses**: `type: map` over 6 lens elements (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope, sre); advisory only, `max_parallel: 4`

- Per-stage `stage_timeout_s` values range from 30s (release) to 5400s (test); per-call `router.timeout_s` values are separate ceilings
